name: Tretinoin
drug_class: Retinoid (retinoic acid receptor agonist; differentiating agent)
route_note: oral capsules for acute promyelocytic leukaemia; topical cream or gel for acne and photoageing
originator: Hoffmann-La Roche (oral, APL); Johnson & Johnson/Ortho (topical Retin-A)

discovery.by: Albert Kligman and James Fulton (University of Pennsylvania), topical acne use; Wang Zhenyi's group (Shanghai), APL
discovery.note: Tretinoin is the active acid form of vitamin A; its use in acute promyelocytic leukaemia was established by Shanghai investigators in the 1980s.

tagline: Vitamin A acid that turned acute promyelocytic leukaemia into a curable disease
summary: Tretinoin (all-trans retinoic acid) is the biologically active form of vitamin A. Orally it induces differentiation of leukaemic promyelocytes in acute promyelocytic leukaemia (APL), and combined with arsenic trioxide it cures most patients; topically it is a long-established treatment for acne and photodamage.
mechanism: In APL, the t(15;17) translocation produces the PML::RARA fusion protein, which represses retinoic-acid target genes and blocks myeloid differentiation. Pharmacological concentrations of tretinoin bind the RARA moiety, release co-repressors and recruit co-activators, and trigger proteasomal degradation of the fusion protein, so the blasts mature into granulocytes.
In skin, activation of nuclear retinoic acid receptors normalises follicular keratinisation, reduces microcomedones and increases epidermal turnover and collagen synthesis.
uses: Induction of remission in acute promyelocytic leukaemia (with arsenic trioxide and/or anthracycline chemotherapy)

history.title: Topical acne treatment
history.detail: Kligman and colleagues report topical tretinoin for acne.

history.title: Retin-A approved
history.detail: FDA approves topical tretinoin for acne.

history.title: APL remissions
history.detail: Huang Meng-er, Wang Zhenyi and colleagues in Shanghai report complete remissions in APL with oral ATRA (Blood 1988).

history.title: PML::RARA
history.detail: The t(15;17) fusion is shown to involve the retinoic acid receptor alpha gene.

history.title: Vesanoid approved
history.detail: FDA approves oral tretinoin (Roche) for APL.

history.title: APL0406
history.detail: Lo-Coco et al. show ATRA plus arsenic trioxide is superior to ATRA plus chemotherapy in low- to intermediate-risk APL.

pk.half_life: about 0.5–2 hours (oral); induces its own metabolism
pk.bioavailability: oral well absorbed, increased with food

safety.boxed_warning: Oral tretinoin: boxed warning for differentiation syndrome, leukocytosis and embryo-fetal toxicity; use only by physicians experienced with APL.

facts: APL went from one of the most rapidly fatal leukaemias to having cure rates above 90% in low-risk disease with ATRA plus arsenic trioxide.
